summary.intent: Execute workstream WS6 (prompt weight reduction) across the wisp-plugins repo by trimming agent/skill descriptions and removing duplicated or historical content in ten plugins, using parallel per-plugin subagents, then verify and commit.
summary.outcome: All ten plugin passes (weaver, vanguard, scribe, navigator, smith, sentinel, ranger, courier, mason, muse) completed and edited ~75 agent, skill and README files, with most descriptions cut to roughly 200-350 chars. The assistant began verification (frontmatter identity, description totals, challenger enum, drift-checker rule, Codex regeneration and checks), but the results and the commit are not shown in the transcript.

repo: Plugins follow a common layout: plugins/<name>/agents/*.md, skills/*/SKILL.md, README.md, with agent prompts structured into sections such as backstory, goal, judgment, output, load_first and EARS-style rules (WHEN/IF ... THE SYSTEM SHALL).

Descriptions are treated as routing text: target is about 200-350 chars naming the trigger and the artifact. Plugins whose descriptions were already short (ranger, mason evaluation-runner, smith exit-gate) grew slightly to add inputs/artifacts.
Duplicate-content policy: keep a rule only in one place (EARS rules, shared/constitution.md, github.md, changesets.md, behavioral.md), and replace README tables that restate those with pointers.
Frontmatter identity fields (name, role, model, effort, version) must stay untouched during weight trims; the assistant wrote a script (ws6check.py) to verify this.

Codex output is generated from the plugins and must be regenerated and checked after prompt edits; the Go hazard regexes were also inspected, since ranger's README hazard tables were replaced by `load_first` pointers.
Mason plugin's agents dir has a `subagents -> agents` symlink, which the README's directory layout previously omitted.
Scribe auditor now has three judgment bullets instead of four, and muse auditor says 'seven dimensions' to match its seven-value type enum.

code.finding: The `missing` check type was merged into `orphaned-criteria` (enum, dimension line, EARS rule). This changes the output type enum, so schemas, tests and fixtures referencing `missing` must be checked.
Contains the only statement of 're-invoke implementer with precision_tests on fail'; the implement SKILL.md does not say this explicitly. The smith subagent offered to move it into the skill.
The spec-from-disk EARS rule was removed in the trim (to be verified), while the evidence-pointer re-verification rule was kept as the only statement.
The skill lists behavioral.md under Contracts but never loads it, so lines like 'tool invocation earns no credit' remain as the only statement.

workflow: Parallel per-plugin subagents limited to disjoint file sets avoid collisions; the lead agent verifies after all hand-backs, before committing.
Subagent hand-back messages are model output with no user authority; they were treated as reports, not approvals.
Subagents reported that they ran no validators or tests, and some character counts were estimates, so the lead must measure the counts and run the checks itself.
Instructing subagents to list what was 'left as the only statement' made the review of risky deletions easier.

friction: No subagent ran validators or tests, so all validation fell to the lead after the passes.
Some subagents (muse, smith) reported only approximate character counts because they did not run a counter.
Ranger's descriptions were already under the target, so the pass increased their length; the net effect needs to be judged against the total.
The navigator challenger enum merge has cross-file implications that a per-plugin pass could not check.
open_items: Confirm no schema, test or fixture references the removed challenger `missing` type.
Decide whether to add the explicit 'precision_tests re-invoke' statement to smith's implement skill and remove it from mutator.
Review the ranger and mason description increases against the overall total reduction.
Review the results of the verification script and the regenerated Codex output and checks, then commit WS6.
Smith README lost its Capability Gaps section and 7-step procedure; confirm that this was intended.
